one_star_reviews.text:
I visited the Polo Ralph Lauren DFO store today to exchange the colour of a top that I had purchased only two days ago.

The exchange was processed correctly and professionally, so I have no complaint about the transaction itself. However, I felt that the staff member was eager to finish the interaction and have me leave as quickly as possible. I did not feel welcomed or valued as a customer.

What disappointed me most is that it reinforced an impression I have had about this type of retail environment: that customers seem to receive a much warmer and more welcoming attitude when staff believe they are about to spend more money.

I understand that staff can be busy or may simply have had a difficult day, so I don't want to make assumptions about the employee's intentions. Nevertheless, the experience left me uncomfortable and disappointed. Good customer service should make a customer feel respected whether they are making a large purchase, exchanging an item, or simply asking for assistance.

I hope this feedback can be taken constructively and used to reinforce the importance of making every customer feel welcome.

Cons: The main con is the terrible cancellation experience. You can be a member since 2023 but they will enforce the contract terms and fine print for commercial gain over customer experience.

In my case, I'm paying for 1 payment after my first cancellation request + another 28 days of notice on top of that despite being provided incorrect information earlier from another staff member. I also haven't used the facilities in some time either - or plan to.

Common sense says theres no actual cost to terminating my access in this digital world. Theres no real need to cover any "manual" admin costs to canceling.

Not acting in Good Will after this tenure simply feels like a last minute cash grab, which I concede is fair, I signed.

"Cancellation has been processed in accordance with the terms and conditions of your membership", at the end of the day this is management's discretion like any other business. Fair sure, happy with the outcome, no.

Pros: Gym is clean & quite big with great people attending.

Conclusion:

Clean Gym, Great people, Good equipment.

If you're a night owl, not the gym for you.

Great if you live near by & make frequent visits with short sessions to fit between getting off work & 11pm.

I would mark out 28 days of notice on your calendar behind every renewal or plan ahead as One55 will subject you to contract terms regardless of your membership period.

Personally for me, my cancellation experience means I won't be coming back, so one star. That's my opinion.

Previous to cancelling i'd give it 3.5 to 4 stars, sighting opening hours as an area for improvement.

Very disappointed with the way this has been handled.

one_star_reviews.text: The 5*’s are fake!!!! The 1*s are legit!!   Booked a course with APM via Work Australia. They called and asked if I could rebook the course (same date, time, location, content) as they had amended the course ID code and needed me to book the option with the new code, then they dropped ‘as per the email we sent you’. Like chuck I ched! I usually respond to email, double checked the address, their area manager had done a typo on the email addy….not to worry, these things happen, some people  don't habitually ‘review before sending’ external comms, all good. I was told they'd send me instructions on how to get rid of the old course and to book in the new one. The PDF they sent was a workflow for a different system, so wasn't helpful. Thought id give it a crack on my own, to find the course no longer available at all, never mind with an amended code. . Emailed APM to advise, had to lock in a much later in October course, as I needed to show workforce I had something booked. No response from APM. Discovered today a new course, similar content, slightly different description, date is two weeks earlier than the alternative I was forced to book. Great, ill change to the new earlier date course. After jumping through hoops at the circus, turns out APM still had me booked in the first, original course, the code hadnt been updated and it started last week. ‘Ahhhhhh did you perhaps notice that I wasn't there’ I asked and then realised if I waited for an answer, I was placing myself in a trigger zone, a direct contradiction to my perception of said providers competence…..I have to let other people know to avoid these champions I thought, and flew to googleopolous. I see everyone else has similar tales to mine, apart from 4 people,  who appear to have struck it lucky with their (no longer at APM) coordinator. Interestingly, all other five stars for this company are from people who have only ever made 1 review (apm) or a couple of other reviews for other businesses with their APM 5* review having no comments at all…outstanding five stars rating and you have nothing at all to say about it????? ODD AS EFF..Guessing someone in their customer engagement team thought fake five star reviews were the way to go….. perhaps Ive managed to dodge a bullet prior to commencing any course with them, hoping I have time to find a non-dismal provider who has their s@@t together, knows what they're doing and genuinely wants to help me land an earner, recommendations anyone?

one_star_reviews.text:
I found my entire experience with UnitingCare's Family Relationship Centre in Bundaberg & Maroochydore to be extremely disappointing. In my view, the process and its outcome have likely caused lasting harm to my children and our family relationships.

My concerns were significant enough that I lodged a formal complaint with the Australian Government department responsible for funding the service.

I would encourage anyone who believes they have experienced a similar situation, or who feels they have been treated by an unprofessional or biased service, to consider lodging a formal complaint with the relevant government department so their concerns can be independently assessed.

PLEASE NOTE: Serious concerns regarding practitioner qualifications and experience

I am writing because I am deeply concerned about the level of practical experience potentially required before someone can work in a position of significant influence over families going through separation and dispute resolution.

I understand that becoming an accredited Family Dispute Resolution Practitioner includes only 50 hours of practical placement. If correct, I believe every parent using these services should be concerned that someone with relatively limited practical experience (ONLY 50 hours!!!) could be involved in decisions and assessments that may have serious consequences for their family.

This centre deals with families at their most vulnerable — parenting disputes, family violence allegations, child safety concerns and court proceedings. While practitioners are not judges, their assessments, decisions about whether FDR proceeds, and the issuing of section 60I certificates can significantly affect what happens next.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was deeply disappointed and profoundly upset by my experience with this church, particularly in my interactions with pastor Rob and his wife Chrissy.

What I experienced was, in my view, completely inconsistent with the Christian principles this church professes to uphold. Christianity is supposed to be about love, kindness, compassion, acceptance, grace and treating every person with dignity. Sadly, that is not what I experienced.

I was judged on my appearance, my loving and kind heart was questioned, and I was spoken to in a way that I found cruel, hurtful and completely unacceptable. I found the experience absolutely appalling.

What makes this particularly disappointing is the enormous gap between what is preached and what is practised. It is easy to speak about Christian values from the pulpit, but those values mean very little if they are not demonstrated through the way people are treated.

To me, Christianity cannot simply be lip service. If love, compassion, acceptance and kindness are genuinely at the heart of a church, they should be evident in every interaction — especially when dealing with someone who is vulnerable or simply seeking to be welcomed and treated with respect.

Church leadership carries a responsibility to lead by example. Judging someone’s appearance, questioning the sincerity of their heart, and using words that cause unnecessary hurt is not the experience I would expect from people representing an Anglican Christian church.

I left this experience feeling deeply hurt, judged and profoundly disappointed. I hope the pastor and his wife genuinely reflect on their actions and consider whether the way they treat people reflects the Christian principles they preach.

Christianity should be lived, not simply spoken about.

Some feedback for Victoria at the front desk: a little more professionalism, attentiveness and willingness to assist customers would go a long way.

I came in to ask about my glasses, which have developed a glazing issue and are still under warranty. I was told over the phone that this could be looked into, however when I arrived, Victoria simply told me to go back to the store I originally purchased them from. When I explained that this was not what I had been told over the phone, I was told that dealing with it through them would be a longer process anyway.

She cleaned the glasses, but unfortunately this didn’t resolve the issue, and there didn’t seem to be much effort to investigate it further. I was then told that I could wait 20 minutes for the manager if I wanted to, but I was at work and simply didn’t have time to sit around waiting. Victoria also told me that it wasn’t really worth doing through them anyway, which made me feel as though she simply didn’t want to deal with the issue.

I then asked if I could at least have a replacement cleaning wipe, and was told I would have to pay for one. Considering how expensive the glasses are in the first place, I found this pretty ridiculous.

I completely understand that some issues may require a particular process, but the way this was handled felt dismissive and unhelpful. My advice would be to show a little more interest in assisting customers and a little more professionalism when dealing with issues, particularly when the customer is simply trying to resolve a warranty matter.

I had an eye test at another OPSM branch a couple of months ago and recently visited this branch simply to get a copy of my prescription.

The staff member took my details and was able to access my record and see my prescription, but told me she couldn’t write it down or email me a copy because my eye test had been done at a different OPSM branch. I was told I would need to contact that branch directly instead.

I found this really frustrating and quite disappointing. If my details and prescription are accessible within the OPSM system, I don’t understand why a customer can’t simply be provided with a copy of their own prescription at another branch. What should have been a very simple request became unnecessarily complicated.

Unfortunately, not a great customer service experience.

This is a church where genuine Christian values run head-on into the principles for running a small business purely according to the selfish whims of its owners, and are totally overwhelmed.

Ordinary people who attend the church are treated like customers. So Narwee Baptist Church has an unusually poor leadership culture.

Unfortunately, open sexism dominates the church. And gay people are very unpopular.

So according to the thinking of this church, men who are not up to much are truly extraordinary. Professional women who really can do anything are kept at arm's length. Members of the LBGTQIA+ community are rated further down. At the very bottom of the scale are Christians in the church who extend their care to the members of this community. They are judged extremely harshly.

The people of the church too are strangely aloof, as though in their heads they are always somewhere else. They don't look at you, they look through you. Gossip about you is far more important to most of them than you are, yourself.

Weird, also--the view that marriage is only between a man and a woman is fancied at the church to be a cardinal teaching of Christianity. Most odd! Thus, you can only advance in the church if you accept this silly idea. Of course, it isn't true. C.S. Lewis himself would scoff at it. No devout Christian can agree something no-one ever articulated until the 21st Century is a cardinal teaching of Christianity.

As well as this, Narwee Baptist Church has a long history of ill-treating young women. The leadership culture is so poor, in this respect, that when a seriously disabled person complained recently about an act of intimidation committed in front of them by one of the senior male leaders against a young woman, they were immediately banned out of pure spite from attending Sunday services, under threat of being prosecuted for trespassing if they tried to come along.

There was no meaningful investigation; there was only a pretend one. The guilty person suffered no consequences at all. The poor disabled eyewitness however is still banned from attending church services, to this day - in the name of the physical safety of, and the peace and harmony between, the other church people.

Before that, another senior male leader subjected a young women to months of searching psychological pressure via text messages. When this came out, he was given nothing more than a gentle pat on the wrist, and later when he left the church, he left with fanfare.

Sadly, for this church's senior leaders, that the apple is rotten in the middle is unimportant, seeing that they can still make the skin glow if they polish it hard enough.

Another problem with Narwee Baptist Church is that the senior leaders, for the most part, have a very simple, basic understanding of the biblical message; of life's everyday problems; of how to think well; of how to teach others; and of how to relate properly to people. Their reading skills are unusually poor. This makes for an extremely shallow and very small pond in which to fish for inspiration, for the sake of your own life.

If you are a bossy, self-righteous, not very bright male with not much self-control who struggles to relate with any kindness to women, all your dreams will come true here. If you are not, the reverse will happen.

I’m very disappointed with the service I received cinacotta  Pharmacy at riverstone “Today  my husband was discharged after the second stage of his ankle surgery (ORIF) at Nepean Private Hospital. He was prescribed Endone for severe post-operative pain. When I took the prescription to this pharmacy, the pharmacist said she could not read the doctor’s handwriting. I understand that safety checks are important. However, I was simply told to come back the next day because the prescription could not be read. This left my husband in severe pain without the medication he urgently needed after major surgery.” “What makes this even more disappointing is that the same situation occurred about three months ago after his first ankle surgery at Royal North Shore Private Hospital when I brought the prescription to this same pharmacy and was again told that the doctor’s handwriting could not be read, delaying his medication.” “This is now the second time we have encountered the same problem at this pharmacy. As a result, my husband was left in severe pain after surgery, causing unnecessary stress and distress for our family.”

“While I respect the need to verify prescriptions, I expected better communication, greater urgency, and more assistance for a patient who’d just undergone major surgery. Based on these repeated experiences, I have lost confidence in this pharmacy and will be using a different pharmacy in future. I hope processes are reviewed so other patients and families don’t go through the same thing.”

We had the seafood tower a couple of weeks ago as a bit of a treat after having a little win, and honestly, we were so disappointed.

Instead, the prawns were actually brown in colour, the lobster didn’t taste fresh, and overall the seafood had virtually no flavour.We also encountered gritty bits of sand as we ate the prawns. We didn’t even finish them.” We didn’t even finish the prawns.

I actually asked our waitress whether the seafood had been frozen because it was so noticeable. She confirmed that it had and explained that there was a new chef and that the previous chef used to get the seafood fresh. She actually encouraged me to leave a review about it.

Honestly, the chef should be ashamed of serving seafood of that quality at that price. Something needs to change, because customers paying $120–$130 for a previously frozen seafood tower deserve far better.

There really is no excuse when we live in an area where beautiful fresh seafood is so readily available. You can head down to Chinderah and buy gorgeous fresh seafood, so for a local venue in Kingscliff to serve a seafood tower of this quality while charging premium prices is incredibly disappointing.

We don’t get to treat ourselves to something like this very often, which made it even worse. For us, the seafood tower was honestly about 1/10.

I love supporting local, but when you’re charging premium prices, the quality needs to match. Unfortunately, on this occasion it absolutely didn’t.

Would I recommend the seafood tower at that price? Definitely not. I’d rather head down to Chinderah, buy beautiful fresh seafood and make my own platter at home. 🦐🦞

Such a shame, because with that incredible location, a beautiful fresh seafood tower could be absolutely amazing.

one_star_reviews.text:
When someone passes away, there is rarely clarity or experience at play for the people suddenly responsible for what happens next.

For me, this was my first time calling a funeral home to organise someone to take care of a “body”. The man who had passed away was my friend and colleague, and I was supporting his wife, who is also my friend and colleague, through an incredibly difficult time. I found myself standing alone in a hospital hallway, completely outside my comfort zone, trying to work out what I was supposed to do. I called the first name on the list I was given: Darwin Funeral Services.

**My first mistake.**

As soon as I gave Brendan my friend’s name and home community, it was clear he understood he was dealing with an Aboriginal family. During that first conversation, he told me not to bring the children when the family came in to make arrangements because **“Aboriginal kids throw stones.”**

That was the moment I should have hung up.

For the record, the children he was making assumptions about are better behaved than my own balanda children. The assumption was offensive and completely unnecessary.

When I later brought my friend’s wife, mother and grandmother in to complete paperwork and choose a coffin, I had written his name on a piece of paper specifically so it did not need to be spoken aloud. This cultural consideration was seemingly not understood, and despite my efforts to avoid his name being repeatedly spoken, it continued throughout the conversation. In a place like Darwin, I would have thought this was relatively common knowledge within the funeral industry, particularly for someone with many years of experience working with families across the Top End. The lack of awareness was incredibly disappointing.

There were numerous other moments that demonstrated a lack of cultural understanding. On one occasion I phoned simply to ask about the progress of the coffin. The first response was **“Have they paid?”** — despite the family having paid a considerable time earlier. Given the assumptions already made about this family, that comment sat particularly poorly with me.

The coffin itself was also considerably delayed, with sick leave and jury duty given as explanations. I appreciate that unexpected things happen, but when a grieving family is waiting to take their loved one home, I did not find those delays acceptable. Given everything I had experienced by that point, I couldn't help wondering whether a non-Indigenous family would have received the same level of urgency.

There were positives, and it is only fair that I acknowledge them. The flowers used were good quality, and the assistance provided with NLC and PATS paperwork was genuinely helpful.

Even payment, however, was unnecessarily difficult — there was no EFTPOS facility, which I found extraordinary in 2026.

I imagine this review may be water off a duck’s back. Perhaps Darwin Funeral Services provides a perfectly acceptable service to many Darwin families. I can only speak to what I personally witnessed and experienced.

In my experience, Brendan and Darwin Funeral Services were **not culturally safe**.

If writing this saves even one grieving family from experiencing additional distress at an already devastating time, then I am happy to have written it.

Would I use their services again? **Absolutely not.**

one_star_reviews.text:
If you are considering becoming a Jehovah’s Witness, I strongly encourage you to research the organisation thoroughly before making that decision.

Among the practices and teachings that deserve serious consideration are shunning, restrictions surrounding blood transfusions, and the authority given to a small group of men known as the Governing Body.

Jehovah’s Witnesses practise what they call “disfellowshipping” and have policies that can result in former members being shunned or having their contact with family and friends significantly restricted. For families, this can be deeply painful and, in some circumstances, can result in relationships being severely damaged or even lost.

The organisation also teaches that Jehovah’s Witnesses should refuse blood transfusions, even in circumstances where an individual may otherwise consider a transfusion medically necessary. This is a particularly serious teaching because it can involve life-and-death medical decisions.

The Governing Body exercises central authority over Jehovah’s Witness doctrine and practice. Jehovah’s Witnesses have historically described this group as the “faithful and discreet slave” and as the channel through which Jehovah provides spiritual direction. Critics, former members and some scholars dispute the organisation’s claims of divine authority and argue that this level of religious control can make questioning or leaving extremely difficult.

For anyone researching Jehovah’s Witnesses, I would encourage you to look beyond the organisation’s own publications and investigate the experiences of former members as well.

From my perspective, the combination of strict religious authority, shunning, restrictions concerning blood and the consequences that can follow from leaving raises very serious concerns about the impact on families and individual freedom.

If you are looking for an organisation where questioning its teachings can have profound consequences for your family relationships, I strongly recommend doing your research before getting involved.

I have officially cancelled my membership at EMF North Lakes after a highly frustrating experience. I recently received complaints about lifting heavy weights, specifically regarding making noise and exerting myself during my sets. This is highly disappointing for a gym that markets itself as a premium fitness facility. It is completely unrealistic for a gym to expect total silence during heavy, intense training. Weightlifting requires effort, and policing members who are actually working hard is ridiculous for a fitness facility.

On top of that, the overall atmosphere is really poor. The energy is completely flat because the majority of people are just sitting on arse on the equipment staring at their phones the entire time. It feels less like a motivating training environment and more like a phone booth.

I hope management focuses less on policing members who are actually working hard and more on fostering a better, more active gym culture.

**Reply**
I have been a loyal member of EMF Coomera/Nerang for nearly 10 years and have never received a single complaint during that entire time. Recently, I made a general, reasonable complaint about people sitting on equipment scrolling on the phones without actually training. Shortly after speaking up, I was hit with a " first and second warning" for simply training hard. Management claimed they made the decision to cancel my membership, but that is false. I chose to leave because of how I was targeted. Having visited North Lakes few years ago, it it clearly shows that the atmosphere there has completely changed for the worse. The membership numbers seem to be dropping, and frankly, I don't see this gym lasting long under its current management. It feels like I was directly targeted just for speaking up about gym etiquette.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our child trained here for more than three years, so this isn’t a one-off reaction.

Lion Bushido markets itself on the values of Bushido — respect, integrity, discipline — and calls itself “not just a sport, but a way of life.” That’s exactly why our experience was so disappointing.

We raised concerns about tournament fairness more than once, including in writing, and never received a single reply. After our child was treated unfairly at a recent tournament, we shared our disappointment in good faith. The principal, David Snell, responded with what we can only describe as dismissiveness, hostility and arrogance — he refused to hear the details of what had happened, talked over us, and ordered our family to leave rather than engage with a genuine concern.

An academy that teaches children respect, honesty and fairness should be able to show those same values to the families who trust it. Instead we were met with contempt. We can’t recommend Lion Bushido, and we’d urge other parents to think carefully before enrolling, especially if respect and open communication matter to you.

Extremely disappointed with our experience at Lion Bushido, and unfortunately, I would not recommend this school to others.

We have been training here for four years and have invested a great deal of time, commitment, and trust in this school. However, after participating in a recent tournament, we felt that we were treated unfairly. When we raised concerns about the fairness of the competition, instead of being listened to and treated with respect, we were met with a dismissive and disrespectful attitude.

What hurt and disappointed me most was the response I received when I tried to remind Shihan of our long-standing relationship with the school. I said to him, “Shihan, we’ve been with you for years. We’re old friends, and I don’t think we should be treated like this.” His response to me was simply, “You should go now, go, go!”

After four years of loyalty, trust, and commitment, hearing those words was incredibly disappointing. It made us feel that our years at the school meant very little the moment we questioned something we genuinely believed was unfair.

No student or family should feel afraid to raise a concern or feel that they will be treated differently simply for speaking up. Disagreement can happen anywhere, but the way concerns are handled says a great deal about the values and culture of a school.

Based on our experience, I would strongly encourage parents and prospective students to think carefully before committing to this school. A martial arts school should teach not only skills and discipline, but also fairness, respect, integrity, and sportsmanship. Unfortunately, our experience left us seriously questioning whether those values are being upheld here.

After four years, we never imagined we would walk away feeling this disappointed, dismissed, and disrespected.

one_star_reviews.text:
One star — not simply because my car was damaged, but because concrete fell from above onto it while it was parked in a public car park, and the response afterwards left me with even more concerns.

On 26 June 2026, I parked my car in the underground car park at Channel Court Shopping Centre. When I returned a few hours later, I found the windscreen shattered and the roof and bonnet damaged after concrete had fallen from the structure above onto my stationary vehicle.

The thought that has stayed with me ever since is very simple: what if a person had been standing there instead of my car?

By the time I returned, the fallen concrete had already been removed. When I discovered the damage, I could not see warning signs, barricades, or closed parking bays around the affected area.

I contacted security immediately and subsequently dealt with Channel Court Centre Management / Angaet Property Management.

I asked for practical assistance regarding the safety of the damaged vehicle, towing, arranging an assessment, alternative transport, and insurer or claims information. NO practical assistance was provided with towing, arranging the assessment, alternative transport, or insurer/claim details, and I ultimately had to arrange and pay for the towing and assessment myself.

Centre Management later denied liability and described what happened as an “unexpected failure of concrete.”

I understand that legal liability is disputed, and I am not asking people reading a Google review to decide who is legally responsible. That is a separate matter.

What I can fairly review is my own experience of how the situation was handled after a serious and unusual incident on premises open to the public.

For me, the most disappointing part was not simply the financial loss. It was that after concrete had fallen onto my car, I received very little practical support and found it difficult to understand what had happened, what follow-up had taken place, and what steps had been taken regarding safety.

I also want to be fair: I do not know the engineering cause of the concrete failure. Those are technical questions for the appropriate professionals and authorities.

But when concrete falls from above in an area routinely used by the public, I believe the response should leave the affected person, and ideally the wider community, confident that safety, transparency and practical support are being taken seriously.

Unfortunately, that was not how this experience felt to me.

A damaged car can eventually be repaired or replaced. What is much harder to forget is the thought that, had somebody been standing beside it at that moment, this could have been a very different story.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointed with my experience.

I have an extremely intense needle phobia, and it took me around 10 years to build up the courage to have a blood test. I explained how scared I was, so I found the way I was treated incredibly upsetting.

When I was taken into the room, a group of staff gathered outside the door and were laughing while I was crying. When it was time to take my blood, the staff member performing the procedure yelled out, “Come and hold her down.” I was not being uncooperative or trying to pull my arm away, I was simply extremely frightened and struggling with my fear. Hearing this while already in such a vulnerable state was incredibly distressing and in my opinion completely inappropriate.

Before I had even had a chance to calm down, the staff member was putting the blood tubes in front of my face so I could check the information. I understand that I needed to confirm the details, but given how distressed I was, I would have appreciated being given even a moment to compose myself first.

I had worked incredibly hard to overcome my fear enough to attend this appointment, and unfortunately this experience has left me even more terrified about having another blood test in the future.

People with a severe needle phobia can be extremely vulnerable in this situation, and I feel this was handled with very little empathy or professionalism. I would not recommend this pathology based on my experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience studying my course at this TAFE was extremely disappointing, and I would not choose to study there again.

The biggest issue was the lack of organisation and communication. There were ongoing problems with the network, yet when the system wasn’t working, students were often blamed rather than the issue being properly escalated to IT. Communication from teachers was also extremely poor.

Emails would go unanswered, there was no clear or reliable way to contact staff or the TAFE when you needed assistance, and there was often no proper timetable or clear structure. Everything felt disorganised and unnecessarily difficult.

I also had serious concerns about the standard of some of the practical teaching and assessment. While there were some genuinely good teachers, I felt that others were rushing students through assessments and allowing people to pass when they did not appear to have demonstrated the knowledge or practical skills required to safely work in a healthcare environment.

This is particularly concerning in a health care course. These are not simply academic skills where getting something wrong has no consequences. Students are being prepared to work with vulnerable people, including elderly and dementia patients, and they need to leave their course genuinely competent and confident in what they are doing.

During placement, I also witnessed behaviour from one teacher towards dementia patients that I found extremely unprofessional and inappropriate. I felt that the teacher was provoking patients rather than demonstrating the patience, respect and person-centred approach that should be expected when working with people living with dementia. That was one of the most upsetting aspects of my experience.

Overall, the lack of organisation, communication and consistency in teaching and assessment made this one of the worst educational experiences I have had.

If you are considering studying a course, I would strongly recommend researching your options carefully and speaking to current or former students before enrolling. I personally would not return to this TAFE. Save yourself the trouble.

one_star_reviews.text:
I delayed writing this review because revisiting my father’s experience has been deeply painful. However, I felt it was important to share our experience not only in honour of my father, but for all families facing the incredibly difficult decision of entrusting their loved one’s care to a residential facility. If our story helps even one person or family feel more informed, supported, or empowered to advocate for better care, then sharing it has been worthwhile.

I mainly visited my father in the afternoons and remained with him until late each evening. During this time, I observed significant differences in care standards, communication, and the overall environment between shifts. I acknowledge that some nurses and carers showed compassion, dedication, and genuine concern for residents. However, over time, I became increasingly concerned about inconsistencies in care practices, supervision, and accountability.

My concerns are not based on isolated incidents, but on a consistent pattern of observations relating to gaps in processes, missed opportunities for timely intervention, and inconsistencies in the delivery of appropriate standards of care. I would like to outline several specific examples to provide context and assist in identifying areas requiring review and improvement. These matters raise significant concerns regarding the adequacy of care provided and, in certain circumstances, had the potential to result in serious adverse outcomes.

From his first day, basic hygiene standards were unacceptable. His bathroom was unclean, with a soiled toilet, dried residue in the sink, faecal traces on toilet paper, a mould-covered urinal bottle, and a leaking toilet that remained unrepaired despite repeated reports. When these concerns were raised, I was incorrectly advised that the bathroom was shared. I also witnessed residents’ towels being used to clean contaminated water from the leaking toilet, raising serious infection control concerns.

I also observed misinformation regarding continence care, refusal of hygiene assistance, and my father’s nurse call buzzer being disconnected overnight on several occasions, leaving him unable to call for help. His room remained excessively cold until repeated requests were made. I also witnessed other vulnerable residents waiting for assistance, including one bedbound resident being refused a simple sandwich despite food being available.

Our greatest concern was the failure to recognise and escalate my father’s deteriorating condition. His wounds worsened despite specialist reviews, he developed significant swelling, struggled to breathe when lying flat, and spent nights sleeping upright in a chair. These warning signs were repeatedly dismissed by nursing staff and the facility doctor, and our family was not adequately informed. Only after my sister insisted on a medical review during his final week did a locum doctor identify his condition as an emergency and express concern that it had not been recognised earlier.

I was disappointed to learn that, rather than engaging with the legitimate issues I raised regarding my father’s care, my advocacy was met with negative characterisation. Throughout his care, I remained respectful, professional, and appropriately assertive when I witnessed circumstances that compromised his dignity, safety, or wellbeing.

It became increasingly apparent that, instead of addressing the substance of these matters and taking appropriate accountability, the focus shifted towards undermining the very person advocating for her father. Care-related issues should be assessed objectively and on their merits, rather than reframed as personal criticism of those who bring them forward. Families should be able to advocate for their loved ones without fear of being personally discredited.

I hope my review is considered in that context and contributes to ensuring every resident receives the dignity, compassion, and respect they deserve.

⭐ 1 Star – Be Very Careful Before Buying a Heat Pod

I want to warn other customers about my experience with the Heat Pod I purchased from Chemist Warehouse Crows Nest.

This is now the second Heat Pod I have had to replace. Unfortunately, the latest one failed just outside the 12-month warranty period. I contacted both Chemist Warehouse and Heat Pod expecting some assistance or accountability, but neither company was willing to take responsibility or provide a satisfactory solution.

After already having to replace one Heat Pod previously, I find this extremely disappointing. When a product fails shortly after the warranty period—particularly when it is the second one I’ve had problems with—I would expect the retailer and manufacturer to at least take the issue seriously and offer reasonable assistance.

Instead, I was left feeling that once the 12 months were over, neither party wanted to know.

I am posting this review to warn other customers. Think carefully before spending your money on this product, and be aware that if you experience a failure after the 12-month warranty, you may find yourself dealing with both the retailer and manufacturer refusing responsibility.

Based on my experience with two Heat Pods, I would not purchase this product again and cannot recommend it.

Parramatta Open: had a deeply disappointing encounter here with a woman wearing glasses and short grey hair who mentioned she holds a senior leadership position within the church (her name is proudly displayed on the board).
Unfortunately, her attitude reflected a profound lack of awareness regarding multiculturalism. Upon seeing that I am Asian, she immediately and patronisingly emphasised the availability of "English conversation classes” in her church. Her tone and body language made it painfully clear that she is stereotyping visitors rather than welcoming them.
Let’s be clear: making assumptions about someone's English proficiency based purely on their ethnicity is a form of implicit discrimination. Before judging others through a biased lens, perhaps she should consider who she is talking to—some of us have completed PhDs and surpassed high-level language proficiencies like IELTS. Assuming your own cultural lens is the only "correct" one goes entirely against what I believe is the true mission of the Catholic Church.
On top of this, the upper level of the church needs serious decluttering / tidying up before opening its doors to the public. A sacred space should be a sanctuary of cleansing energy and grace, entirely free from microaggressions and racism (though I certainly hope outdated stereotypes aren't part of their English conversation class curriculum).
True community leadership requires genuine openness, not prejudice.
More education / re-training is needed in this senior leader.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience

Unfortunately, our experience with The Cheesecake Shop was extremely disappointing. We ordered a cake for an 18th birthday and had shown the cake decorator multiple times exactly what we wanted, including the colour and a 2 tier design. She even took a photo of the reference image, and I left the consultation feeling confident that everything was understood.

When we collected the cake on the day of the party, it was nothing like what we had ordered. It was a single tier cake rather than 2 tiers, and the blue colour was completely different. The fondant was unbelievably thick, with thick layers of it inside the cake as well. We struggled to cut through it even with a serrated knife, it crumbled and made an absolute mess when serving. To make matters worse, the mud cake itself was also very dry, which was particularly disappointing considering the amount we had paid for a custom cake.

The staff working that day were apologetic, which we appreciated, but because the cake decorator wasn’t back until Monday, nothing could be resolved. As it was for an 18th birthday that same day, we had no real option but to take the cake.

What was most disappointing was my conversation with the cake decorator on Monday. Rather than acknowledging the obvious differences, I found her rude and unhelpful, and she insisted that what we received was what we had ordered, despite the reference photo and our previous discussions.

After eventually speaking with the manager, we received a refund of $74.95, which was a little under half of what we had paid.

For such an important milestone birthday, the whole experience was incredibly disappointing. Mistakes can happen, but the quality of the cake and the way the situation was handled afterwards made it much worse. Unfortunately, based on this experience, I would not order a custom cake from here again.

one_star_reviews.text:
Subject: WARNING — SERIOUS CONCERNS REGARDING MANAGEMENT AND CARE ENVIRONMENT

I am extremely concerned about my experience with the current management of this facility, particularly the conduct of the new manager, Pha.

Based on my direct experiences and observations, I consider aspects of the management and communication within the facility to have been deeply unprofessional and inappropriate. The manner in which matters have been handled has significantly undermined my confidence in the facility’s management, governance, and ability to appropriately address concerns raised by residents and their families.

As a direct consequence of these experiences, I am actively exploring transferring my mother to another facility. This is not a decision I have taken lightly. I have 35 years of professional experience and have never encountered a situation in which I have had such serious concerns regarding the conduct and manner in which a facility’s management has dealt with matters affecting a resident and their family.

Formal complaints have been lodged with the relevant regulatory bodies, including the NSW Health Care Complaints Commission (HCCC) and Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA), and I intend to allow the appropriate authorities to independently assess the matters raised.

I also want to make clear that my concerns are not directed at the entire workforce. There are staff members at this facility who have consistently demonstrated compassion, professionalism and genuine commitment to residents. In particular, Marissel, Sara, Ruby and RN Peter have always been excellent in my experience, and I have nothing but praise and appreciation for the care and professionalism they have demonstrated.

I was also deeply concerned by interactions I personally witnessed/heard involving management and staff. The manner of communication raised concerns for me that extend beyond an individual nursing or clinical matter and into broader issues of workplace conduct, organisational governance, staff welfare, professional standards and the treatment of residents and their families.

Given the seriousness of these concerns, I believe the organisation should undertake an appropriate internal investigation and governance review, including consideration of whether its policies, complaint-handling processes, management practices and workplace standards are being appropriately followed.

I strongly encourage the organisation to treat these concerns seriously. I intend to pursue the appropriate formal channels and will continue to advocate for my mother’s safety, dignity, wellbeing and right to appropriate care.

The excellent staff I have encountered deserve recognition. However, the concerns regarding management are sufficiently serious that I cannot presently recommend this facility to other families without qualification.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible experience with the store manager,
on Saturday. His behaviour made me feel unsafe and unwelcome in the store.

I was trying the Uni POSCA pens and followed the instructions on the pens themselves: keep the lid on and shake before use. I noticed that one pen did not have the lid on, so after that I made sure the other lids were securely on before shaking them. I also tried some pens that had already been opened. I believe I was behaving normally, following the product instructions, and not disturbing anyone else.

Suddenly, the store manager, Liam, walked towards me, stopped about 1.5 to 2 metres away, and said, “Can you stop shaking the pens? The paint will go everywhere.” He may also have said “thank you.”

I explained that the instructions said the pens should be shaken, and I also had the lids on, but he did not listen. I suggested that if the store does not want customers to shake the pens, there should be a sign displayed. He then walked away and pointed at me and said, “I only saw you doing it there.”

I felt he was rude and dismissive, and I became very uncomfortable. I then spoke to another staff member about the situation.

While I was speaking to that staff member, the store manager approached us and said something along the lines of me wasting his staff member’s time.

He then started telling me that he had spoken to me nicely and that I was the rude one. He seemed to expect me to simply say, “Yes, I won’t do it.” I said the conversation was going in circles and that I no longer felt safe or comfortable. He then told me to finish my business quickly and leave.

Later, I saw other customers at the same pen station shaking the pens without the lids on, yet he did not approach them at all.

What this manager demonstrated was a lack of care for customer experience and an attitude that customers should not provide feedback, even when they are following instructions and raising concerns respectfully.

This happened at Officeworks, and I am raising it here as a formal complaint as well. I found the manager’s behaviour intimidating, dismissive, and targeted. I was particularly concerned that I was singled out while others doing the same thing were ignored.

I will be lodging a formal complaint about this store manager’s behaviour towards customers and staff. This kind of behaviour should not be acceptable at Officeworks. If other customers have experienced something similar, I encourage them to call it out and report it.

If store footage is available, I would welcome it being reviewed.

We visited Caboolture Bowl & Mini Golf for my niece’s 6th birthday, hoping to make her day special. Unfortunately, we played one game and that was more than enough to make us feel unwelcome.

From the moment we arrived, we were given the impression that children — and families in general — were not particularly welcome. We sang Happy Birthday to my niece, only to be met with rude comments about the staff having to wipe down the table afterwards. After spending money specifically to celebrate a child’s birthday, it was incredibly disappointing to be made to feel like we were an inconvenience simply for doing something as innocent as singing Happy Birthday.

We were also moved out of the normal bowling alley and into a small room with only four lanes, where the pins were on strings. The venue has definitely gone downhill compared with how it was a few years ago. The facilities themselves could perhaps be overlooked if the customer service and overall attitude towards families were better.

It’s a real shame because this should be the kind of place where kids can celebrate their birthdays and families can have fun without feeling like they’re a burden.

Very disappointing experience and unfortunately somewhere we won’t be returning to.

one_star_reviews.text:
Where do I begin? Firstly, I would like to acknowledge the frontline nursing staff, who were caring, professional, and provided excellent day-to-day support to my mother during her stay.

Unfortunately, beyond this, our experience was deeply disappointing. While the senior nursing staff were courteous and accommodating, they were unable to provide clear or satisfactory responses to significant concerns regarding my mother's care. Communication throughout her admission was poor, with limited information provided about her treatment plan, discharge planning, or measurable care goals. Questions were often left unanswered, leaving both my mother and me feeling uninformed and excluded from important decisions.

A particularly concerning issue was the lack of direct communication regarding changes to my mother's condition and care. Important discussions, including new diagnoses, appeared to be discussed amongst staff before being communicated to us. Patients and their families should be appropriately consulted and informed about matters affecting their care in a timely and transparent manner.

Our experience with the Allied Health team was equally disappointing. Physiotherapy treatments were provided without what appeared to be adequate consultation regarding my mother's medical history and individual circumstances. The Occupational Therapy service was largely absent throughout her stay. Despite not conducting any direct assessments, updates were provided remotely, which raised concerns about the accuracy and quality of the information being relied upon.

The facility itself also requires significant attention. Issues included very cold air conditioning in some rooms, rattling windows, ageing beds and furniture, and water leaks from ceilings. The overall condition of the property did not meet the standard we expected.

Based on our experience, I would not recommend Dorset to others seeking rehabilitation or ongoing care. While the frontline nursing staff deserve recognition for their dedication, the deficiencies in communication, care coordination, allied health services, and facility maintenance made this a highly disappointing experience and, in my view, indicate a significant decline in standards.

one_star_reviews.text:
My partner was seriously injured at this club last weekend, and the way the situation was handled was extremely concerning.

After waiting almost two hours on the ground for an ambulance, I went to follow up and double-check that one had actually been called. We were then told that, despite being led to believe an ambulance had been arranged, the club had never called one.

What is most concerning is the apparent lack of priority given to ALL players safety. Watching club officials spend an hour trying to get the game restarted instead of making sure there was an ambulance coming was an interesting decision. Their poor priorities were also evident in the decision to continue playing the final half an hour remaining after the game had already been stopped for an hour and a half. Having players move to a different field after such a long break, when they were no longer properly warmed up, arguably increased the risk of further injuries.

Based on our experience, I would not recommend this club to anyone who prioritises the health and safety of their players. It was extremely disappointing to feel that winning appeared to take priority over player welfare
